newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Dock to merge with CityFront.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Dock to merge with CityFront.

text.p: Chicago Dock & Canal Trust said Friday it terminated its merger agreement with Newsweb Corp and signed a definitive merger agreement with CityFront Center LLC.
Under the agreement, CityFront will purchase all outstanding common shares of Chicago Dock & Canal for $25.00 per share in cash.
Chicago Dock said it paid a $3.5 million termination fee to Newsweb and reimbursed it up to $750,000 in expenses.

Chicago Dock, a real estate investment trust, has about 5.8 million shares outstanding, resulting in a total value for the CityFront transaction of about $175 million, including assumed liabilities, the trust said.
Newsweb originally offered $21 a share for Chicago Dock & Canal in September, but raised its bid on December 20 to $23 a share. CityFront last week increased its bid to $25 a share from $23.
Chicago Dock & Canal said its merger with CityFront is the subject of certain litigation filed by Newsweb against the trust, its trustees, CityFront and certain related parties.
At a hearing held on December 19 and 20, 1996 in the Circuit Court of Cook County, Illinois, the court declined to issue a preliminary injunction against the CityFront offer, the trust said.
The court reserved consideration of all other claims in the litigation, Chicago Dock said.
The trust also said CityFront entered into an agreement with Newsweb under which Newsweb will dismiss its lawsuit and vote its Chicago Dock shares in favor of CityFront merger.

The merger with CityFront is subject to approval of the trust's shareholders and other customary closing conditions, Chicago Dock said. Chicago Dock said it authorized the cancellation of the special meeting of shareholders originally scheduled for January 9, 1997 to consider the previous merger agreement with Newsweb and it expects a new special meeting to vote on the CityFront merger will be held in the first quarter of calendar 1997.
Chicago Dock said Lehman Brothers acted as financial advisor to the board of trustees and gave a fairness opinion in connection with the transaction.
Shares of Chicago Dock traded off 5/8 at 24-1/4.
